laws.title: Window tint laws in Texas and Utah
laws.subtitle: Official VLT (visible light transmission) limits, applied automatically in our configurator.
laws.txWindshield: Clear UV/IR film (70%+ VLT) or a non-reflective strip above the AS-1 line
laws.utWindshield: Non-reflective strip above the AS-1 line or the top 4 inches
laws.utReflect: Metallic or mirrored finishes not allowed
laws.txMedical: Allowed with a signed physician or optometrist statement
laws.sourceTx: Texas Department of Public Safety — Window tinting standards (TRC §547.613)
laws.sourceUt: Utah Code §41-6a-1635 — Windshield and window tinting standards

items.q: How long does window tint take to cure?
items.a: Usually 3 to 5 days in warm Texas sun, or up to 2 weeks in cooler weather. Keep your windows up for at least 72 hours after installation.

items.q: Is it normal to see small hazy spots or moisture right after installation?
items.a: Yes. The mounting solution evaporates through the film over the first few days, leaving a perfectly clear finish.

items.q: How should I clean tinted windows?
items.a: Use an ammonia-free glass cleaner and a clean microfiber towel. Avoid abrasive pads and ammonia-based sprays.

items.q: What does the lifetime warranty cover?
items.a: Every level covers bubbling, peeling, cracking and fading for as long as you own the vehicle. Our top ceramic levels also include a transferable warranty.

items.q: What is your deposit and cancellation policy?
items.a: Your $50 deposit holds your appointment and goes toward your total. If you cancel at least 24 hours before your appointment, it's refunded automatically.
